pointers.sentence: The autodetector runs it on each migration it has cut, which puts back into a `CreateModel`, where it can, the relations, indexes and constraints the autodetector wrote as operations apart from it (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._optimize_migrations`; [From operations to migrations: dependencies, order and names](dependencies.md)). squashmigrations runs it, unless given `--no-optimize`, on the operations of all the migrations it replaces (`django/core/management/commands/squashmigrations.py:Command.handle`; [Squashed migrations: `replaces` and the squashmigrations command](squashing.md)).

The autodetector runs it on each migration it has cut, which puts back into a `CreateModel`, where it can, the relations, indexes and constraints the autodetector wrote as operations apart from it (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._optimize_migrations`; [From operations to migrations: dependencies, order and names](dependencies.md)). squashmigrations runs it, unless given `--no-optimize`, on the operations of all the migrations it replaces (`django/core/management/commands/squashmigrations.py:Command.handle`; [Squashed migrations: `replaces` and the squashmigrations command](squashing.md)).

`makemigrations --update`, which folds new operations into an application's last migration, runs it on the lengthened list (`django/core/management/commands/makemigrations.py:Command.write_to_last_migration_files`; [The makemigrations command](makemigrations.md)).

The optimizer calls `Operation.reduce` on one operation with another that stands later in the list, and with the label of the list's application, which an operation does not hold (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.reduce`).

`MigrationOptimizer.optimize` calls `MigrationOptimizer.optimize_inner` on the list, and again on what that returned, until a call returns a list equal to the one it was given (`django/db/migrations/optimizer.py:MigrationOptimizer.optimize`); its docstring draws the consequence, that a fold must never return a list longer than what it replaces.
In a pass, `optimize_inner` takes each operation in turn and asks it about every operation after it, nearest first (`django/db/migrations/optimizer.py:MigrationOptimizer.optimize_inner`).

`ModelOperation.reduce` answers with `Operation.reduce`'s list where there is one, and otherwise with `ModelOperation.can_reduce_through`: true exactly when the later operation's `references_model`, asked about this operation's model, says no (`django/db/migrations/operations/models.py:ModelOperation.reduce`).
`CreateModel.reduce` has a fold for each of these operations on its own model (`django/db/migrations/operations/models.py:CreateModel.reduce`).

`ModelOptionOperation.reduce`, which the operations that alter a model's options or its managers inherit, answers an operation of its own class on its model, or a `DeleteModel` of it, with a list of the later one alone (`django/db/migrations/operations/models.py:ModelOptionOperation.reduce`).

`FieldOperation.reduce` answers with `Operation.reduce`'s list where there is one, and otherwise with true exactly when the later operation's `references_field`, asked about this operation's field, says no (`django/db/migrations/operations/fields.py:FieldOperation.reduce`).

`IndexOperation`, the base of the operations on indexes and constraints, declares none of `reduce`, `references_model` and `references_field` (`django/db/migrations/operations/models.py:IndexOperation`).

`Operation.references_model` returns `True` by the rule in its docstring: if in doubt, return true, since a true too many makes the optimizer a little less efficient and a false too many may leave an optimized migration that cannot be used (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.references_model`); `Operation.references_field` falls back on it.

optimizemigration takes an application's label and a migration's name, or the beginning of one (`django/core/management/commands/optimizemigration.py:Command.handle`, `django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader.get_migration_by_prefix`).
